topic: How do AI models get smarter?
opening: Zoe's robot calls every apple a cookie, and you can spot the fix.
ending: Smart grows one tiny gear turn at a time.

opening: You can help Leo solve a mystery that fits on a fingertip.
ending: Yes or no, super fast, all inside one small chip.
story: Leo's delivery truck and its tiny roads / computer chip = a tiny town of roads where little deliveries zoom; switch (transistor) = a little gate on the road that opens or shuts; on and off = gate open means yes, gate shut means no

opening: By the end, you'll know why Mia's team of friends wins.
ending: Every time you fix an oops, you learn like Mia's team.
story: sorting apples from Zoe's apple tree / neuron = one friend who checks just one small thing about an apple, like its color or its spots; connection weights = how much each friend listens to the friend next to them; training = practicing on a hundred apples and fixing the listening after every mistake; neural network = the whole team of friends passing their guesses down the line

opening: One cup used to cost one coin, and you can find out what changed.
ending: Next time a price jumps, ask: costs or crowds?
story: Mia's lemonade stand on a busy street / cost = the coins Mia pays for lemons, cups and jars; demand = a long line of kids with lots of coins, all wanting lemonade; inflation = when prices at every stand on the street go up together

topic: How can a busy shop still run out of money?
opening: Follow the coins with Mia, and you'll catch the sneaky leak.
ending: It wins when more coins come in than go out.
story: Mia's busy pizza shop / revenue = the coins that come in when friends buy slices; costs = the coins that go out for cheese, boxes and the shop itself; profit = the coins still left in the jar at the end of the day

topic: Can an AI get in trouble with the law?
opening: When a robot spills, who mops up? You're about to find out.
ending: Behind every robot is a person who can fix it.
story: Zoe's robot workshop / AI = Zoe's robot that follows the chip she put inside it; the law = the workshop rules about who fixes a mess; responsible = the people who built it, switched it on and let it roll

topic: How can a game draw fewer dots but look sharper?
opening: Leo's rocket game drew less but looks better, and you get to crack why.
ending: A quick rough picture plus smart guesses makes a sharp sky.
story: the kids' rocket club and its pretend space game / graphics chip = the tiny chip in the rocket that draws the space game; pixels = the little dots that make up every picture on the screen; low resolution = a quick rough picture made with fewer dots; AI upscaling = a smart helper in the chip that has seen lots and lots of pictures and guesses the missing dots

topic: Why don't AI builders fully understand their AI?
opening: Zoe built a robot, but even Zoe can't say how it thinks!
ending: Builders grow AI, so they study it to understand it.
story: picking apples from the apple tree in Zoe's garden / AI = Zoe's robot, whose brain grew like a little tree; training = giving the robot lots of practice, like water and sun for a seed; AI builders = Zoe, who helped the brain grow but never placed each branch; studying the AI = peeking at the branches afterward to see how it learned

opening: Here's how a 2-coin top ends up costing 10.
ending: Hope can lift a price, but only worth holds it up.
story: a spinning top for sale at Leo's toy shop / price = the coins someone pays Leo for the spinning top; real value = how much the top is worth just for spinning it, about 2 coins of fun; money bubble = when the top's price floats way above its fun, only because everyone hopes someone else will pay even more tomorrow; the bubble popping = the day nobody will pay more, so the price drops back to about

topic: When does an AI-edited photo become a fib?
opening: Mia's letters to Grandma hold the answer.
ending: Clearer is honest; better than real is a fib.
story: Ava's photo letters to Grandma's house / AI photo editing = the smart helper on Ava's phone that can change her photos before she mails them to Grandma; touch-up = fixing the light or tidying the edges so Grandma sees Ava's real garden more clearly; fake (a fib) = adding a tree or a door that was never really there, so the photo tells Grandma something untrue; the honesty test = asking: if Grandma

topic: Why can one computer problem stop the whole world?
opening: Raj’s truck carries the key that opens the city hub.
ending: If a system depends on one piece, it can halt.
story: Leo's delivery truck / single point of failure = one broken truck that stops all deliveries; redundancy = extra backup truck / If a system depends on one piece, that piece failing can halt everything.

topic: What does it mean when an economy grows?
opening: Follow Kim's clues, and you'll finally get it when the news says it.
ending: Not pricier ones, just more of them to share.
story: Mia's cookie bakery and the street around it / economy = all the cookies, boxes and work made on Kim's street, added up together; economic growth = the street making more real stuff this year than last year; real growth vs. higher prices = more cookies at the same price is growth; the same cookies at a higher price is not / An economy grows when a place makes more real goods and services than befo

topic: How does AI hear your voice?
opening: The robot that wins this race listens the way your phone listens to you.
ending: It listens in pieces, then picks what makes sense.
story: Zoe's robot workshop, where two robots race to understand Mia / sound waves = the tiny wiggles Mia's voice makes in the air, which the robot's ear feels like ripples in water; breaking sound into slices = the new robot chopping Mia's words into a hundred tiny bits of sound, like slicing a loaf into thin pieces; speech recognition = the robot's chip matching each tiny bit to a sound it has practice
